text:
Let me breathe for a long, long time the scent of your hair; let me plunge my face into it like a thirsty man into spring water, and wave it with my hand like a fragrant handkerchief, to shake memories into the air.

If you could know all I see! All I feel! All I hear in your hair! My soul travels through perfume as other men’s souls travel through music.

Your hair contains an entire dream, full of sails and masts; it contains vast seas whose monsoons carry me toward enchanting climates where space is bluer and deeper, where the air is perfumed by fruit, leaves, and human skin.

In the ocean of your hair I glimpse a harbor teeming with melancholy songs, vigorous men of every nation, and ships of every shape, their fine and intricate architectures outlined against an immense sky where eternal heat lounges at ease.

In the caresses of your hair I find again the languors of long hours spent on a divan in the cabin of a beautiful ship, rocked by the harbor’s imperceptible sway, among flowerpots and cooling jars.

In the glowing hearth of your hair I breathe the odor of tobacco mingled with opium and sugar; in the night of your hair I see the infinity of tropical blue shine; on the downy shores of your hair I grow drunk on the combined scents of cotton, musk, and coconut oil.

Let me bite your heavy black braids for a long time. When I nibble your elastic, rebellious hair, it seems to me that I am eating memories.

translation.title: A Hemisphere in a Head of Hair
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of Baudelaire. The repeated synesthetic voyages through scent, sound, sight, and touch are preserved.
